semantic_changes: Per-node timing instead of one shared Config: bootstrapped leader HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; the two far voters 3s; the near node 6s (all ValidateConfig-clean).
Cluster built from explicit nodes (own InmemTransport, InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore, MockFSM per node) with only the leader bootstrapped, so the leader is deterministic instead of elected by race.
Added a second VerifyLeader call after a competing leader exists, and a write applied through the competing leader with both FSMs sampled.
Added a control case with identical per-node timing in which the near node stays a voter, so the far side is a minority (2 of 4 voters) and no competitor can appear.

scope.description: Extend the observation window of the non-voter VerifyLeader defect: cut a long-lease leader off from the voter majority while one non-voter stays reachable, ask VerifyLeader immediately, then ask again once the majority has elected a competing leader and committed a write.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, VerifyLeader, Apply, GetConfiguration; per-node Config values only, no production code or default changed.

Only the leader is bootstrapped with the four-server configuration (all voters), so it is the only node that can campaign initially; the other nodes start with empty configurations and adopt the configuration through normal AppendEntries replication.

The near node's voter-to-non-voter transition is the public DemoteVoter call; the harness waits until the far side reports it without a vote and records the leader's own view of that suffrage separately from the near node's self view.
Partition is imposed by removing in-memory transport routes in both directions between {leader, near} and the two far voters; the far voters keep their mutual routes.
The 20s leader lease is within ValidateConfig (LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout) and only makes the pre-existing window observable; the defect claim does not rest on the value chosen.
excluded: No TCP or cross-host partition; no disk-backed log/snapshot store.
No change to the target's defaults, and no instrumentation of internal counters.

basis.prefix: Four nodes are created first (identity is the in-memory transport address), then wired fully connected and started; only the first node is bootstrapped with the configuration {leader, near, far1, far2} all Voter, so it wins the initial election and replicates the configuration to the others (they start empty and cannot campaign). The harness waits for the bootstrapped node to be Leader, then for the treatment calls DemoteVoter(near) and waits until both far nodes report the near node without a vote. It emits a setup CA_EVENT carrying the leader's configuration summary (voters, nonvoters, quorum_size, near_node_voter from the leader's view, near_node_self_voter) and the per-node timings. It then removes the transport routes between {leader, near} and {far1, far2} in both directions, emits a partition event, and calls the public VerifyLeader on the partitioned leader (3s deadline for the treatment, 45s for the control). It polls the two far nodes for a Leader state for up to 15s; if one appears it emits verify_while_superseded with the second VerifyLeader result plus both nodes' states, applies 'assurance-superseded-write' through the competing leader, and emits stale_write with the applied index, the state of both FSMs and the old leader's state. The control repeats the identical construction and timing without the demotion.
basis.requirement: A success from VerifyLeader is a confirmation that the caller may keep treating this node as leader and read its FSM (api.go:880-882 documents that purpose). Since non-voters are, by the target's own definition, 'not considered for elections or commitment purposes' (configuration.go:16-18), the confirmation must rest on acknowledgements from a quorum of voters; a non-voter's acknowledgement may not substitute for one.
basis.responsibility: Leader-side quorum confirmation consumed by clients through VerifyLeader, and the leader-lease step-down path that is supposed to bound how long such a confirmation can be wrong.

comparisons.description: The partitioned long-lease leader, able to reach only the demoted non-voter, answers VerifyLeader with success before any competitor exists.

Decisive extension of the anomaly: the same confirmation succeeds again while a competing leader already holds leadership on the voter-majority side, i.e. the confirmation outlives the election the lease is supposed to bound.

A write committed by the competing leader is absent from the old leader's FSM while that old leader still reports Leader, i.e. a client that gates reads on the confirmed leadership reads state missing a committed write.
Control with identical per-node timing but the near node still a voter: the far side is a minority, so no competitor can appear and the same call must not report success.

semantic_changes: Added applicability_conditions {case eq nonvoter_reachable} to comparison 0, {case eq control_same_set_voter} to comparison 1 and {case eq control_nonvoter_unreachable} to comparison 2, so each event comparison applies only to its own case.

before.description: Real 4-node in-memory cluster: elect a leader, optionally move one follower from voter to non-voter via the public DemoteVoter API, partition the cluster so the leader keeps only that node reachable, then call the public VerifyLeader API and record the future result together with the leader state. Treatment keeps a demoted (non-voter) node reachable; control 1 keeps the same reachable set but that node is still a voter; control 2 keeps the demoted non-voter but cuts the leader from every other node. On a successful confirmation the harness also waits for a leader on the far side, applies a write through the new leader and samples both FSMs.
assumptions: Real target constructors are used: BootstrapCluster + NewRaft, InmemTransport fully connected, InmemSnapshotStore, MockFSM; membership change and partition are driven only through public APIs (DemoteVoter) and the in-memory transport's documented Disconnect.

Partitions are established by removing transport routes (cluster.Disconnect / cluster.Partition helpers), i.e. the same mechanism the target's own tests use; the partition set is chosen by the harness, not by the measured result.
Timing: HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout (3s for the treatment attempts, 2s for the controls), CommitTimeout = 50ms, ProtocolVersion 3, so ValidateConfig holds for every node.

The treatment is attempted up to three times because whether a voter-majority election lands inside the partitioned leader's remaining lease window is timing dependent; the VerifyLeader result itself is recorded for every attempt.
excluded: Real TCP transports and cross-process partitions are not exercised; the in-memory transport is the target's own test transport.
No production code, configuration default or store behaviour is modified.

prefix.before: The harness builds each cluster with MakeClusterCustom (Bootstrap: true, LongstopTimeout 60s) so all four nodes are bootstrapped with the same 4-voter configuration, then waits for a stable single leader and its followers. For the treatment and control 2 it calls leader.DemoteVoter(nearNode.localID, 0, 10s) and waits until the far side reports the node without a vote, so the leader's own quorum size is 2 of voters {leader, far1, far2}. It then partitions the cluster with cluster.Partition([leader, nearNode]) (treatment, control 1) or cluster.Disconnect(leader) (control 2), records the setup and partition as CA_EVENT lines, launches leader.VerifyLeader().Error() in a goroutine and polls the far side for a Leader state while waiting for the result. The result, the leader's state, elapsed time and whether another leader existed are emitted as a verify_result CA_EVENT. If the confirmation succeeded, the harness waits up to 4s for a far-side leader, applies 'assurance-stale-write' through it, and emits stale_read_window with both FSMs' contents, the leader's state and the applied index.

responsibility.before: Leader-side quorum confirmation consumed by the client through the public VerifyLeader API; the leader owns both the quorum arithmetic (quorumSize, voter-filtered) and the vote attribution (verifyFuture.vote, unfiltered) that decide the answer.
responsibility.after: Leader-side quorum confirmation consumed by clients through VerifyLeader, and the leader-lease step-down path that is supposed to bound how long such a confirmation can be wrong.

before.description: Anomaly prediction for the treatment: the leader that can reach only the demoted non-voter answers VerifyLeader with success (nil error) while its quorum size of 2 is defined over voters {leader, far1, far2}. Satisfying this comparison supports the defect explanation; it does not by itself establish it.

Control 1 (only the suffrage of the reachable node differs): with that node still a voter the leader must not report success, because its acknowledgement belongs to the quorum that is otherwise unreachable.
Control 2 (only reachability differs): with the same non-voter suffrage but no reachable peer at all, no acknowledgement can arrive, so success must not be reported.

after.description: The partitioned long-lease leader, able to reach only the demoted non-voter, answers VerifyLeader with success before any competitor exists.

Decisive extension of the anomaly: the same confirmation succeeds again while a competing leader already holds leadership on the voter-majority side, i.e. the confirmation outlives the election the lease is supposed to bound.

Control with identical per-node timing but the near node still a voter: the far side is a minority, so no competitor can appear and the same call must not report success.

revision_reason: Same cause and investigation, new timing basis and an extended observation endpoint: per-node Config values (20s leader lease vs 3s voting peers) let the voter majority elect its own leader well before the partitioned leader's lease expires, which the shared-timing harness could not achieve. The harness file is replaced accordingly (new scenario, same helpers).
